title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games
metadata_mismatch: Read v4. Metadata abstract (earlier version) gives '84.1-100%' at one-ply tactics; v4 reports 84.9% and 100%. Author spelled 'Garrido Merchán' in paper vs 'Garrido-Merchán' in metadata.
why_wsp: An LLM (Claude Sonnet 5, plus other models in replications) writes every weight of feed-forward game-playing networks from the rules, with no gradient descent or training data, and the networks are checked against independent oracles.
domain: two-player games (Nim, Wythoff, tic-tac-toe, Dots and Boxes, Connect Four, Othello, KRK/KQK chess endgames)
editor: Claude Sonnet 5 (main ladder, Track A); replications by Codex ('6 Luna High', identity unverified), Grok 4.7 High, Claude Opus 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, second Sonnet 5; Track B open-weight Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B, Qwen3 4B, Ministral 8B
target: ten hand-set ReLU feed-forward networks, 3,786 (Wythoff) to 38,898,084 (KQK) parameters (Table 7)
interface: code/tensor tools (Track A: code execution, own test suites, exhaustive-search tooling); Track B: single cold text reply with module, no tools
loop: Track A: closed-loop with feedback (self-testing, offline exhaustive solve, override per disagreement); Track B: one-shot
self_editing: no; editor writes separate small networks
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all weights written from scratch: 'every network holds zero trainable parameters' (Table 7 caption)

headline_results.claim: Six of ten networks exact under exhaustive check vs independent oracle
headline_results.quote: Six of the ten networks are correct by exhaustive search against independently written oracles

headline_results.claim: Nim network agrees with oracle on all states with 4,323 parameters, zero overrides
headline_results.quote: Nim, 3 piles 512 0 4323 512/512 never loses from any of the 448 winning states

headline_results.claim: Chess endgame collapse from one-ply tactic to full game
Standard boards: strong vs random, lose all games vs search
headline_results.quote: Against search, both networks lose every game in both seats, with no exception across 1600 games in total.

headline_results.claim: Open-weight models up to 8B fail Nim under cold protocol
headline_results.quote: No arm reached a second block. All five stopped on Nim

headline_results.claim: Verification-habit prompt addendum did not help
headline_results.quote: Table 10 shows no rung on which the addendum helped.

cost.claim: Verification wall-clock per network (not construction cost), 16-core CPU
Track B token use for open-weight arms
cost.quote: stopped of its own accord after one thousand one hundred and forty-five tokens of an eight-thousand-token budget

baselines_and_controls: independent from-scratch oracles (backward induction, retrograde tablebases validated against external counts); random and alpha-beta search opponents (depth 2-4); a policy with the same hand-set evaluation plus two plies of search; cross-model replications; paired with/without prompt addendum; determinism check over 50 loads
runs_and_variance: Statistical rungs: 'ten random seeds and 400 games per condition and side' with Wilson 95% CIs (Sec. 5.4); constructions are single attempts per model; prompt pilot 'a single attempt per condition' (Sec. 5.8)
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning/quantization of written nets); determinism across reloads used as a check on Track B outputs
verification: exhaustive game-tree verification against independent oracles for 6 networks; exhaustive per-position checks against retrograde tablebases for chess endgames; Wilson CIs for standard boards; replication outputs re-run by author
memorization_vs_reasoning: Gate primitives not given in brief but 'rediscovered' by every attempt; worked example is a different game (tic-tac-toe). Track A overrides come from offline exhaustive solving, i.e. tabulation, not derivation. Interpretation of transcripts is flagged as 'not a measurement'.
limitations_stated: Opponent-depth axis not traced as a curve; override counts are upper bounds from one tier vocabulary; cross-constructor evidence mixes administrators, sample sizes and opponent strengths; prompt pilot run from a session holding the manuscript (possible contamination); GPU memory limited doubled ceiling for two largest Track B arms.
code_or_data: released per Sec. 7 (networks, oracles, briefs, Track B harness, pre-registration); no URL found in text
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 (Sparks of weight-space programming blog)
Garrido Merchán 2026 companion: Zero-Shot WSP for prediction/classification on structured datasets
notes_for_survey: Most rigorous verification in the B2 game-writing line: exhaustive oracle checks and a difficulty ladder with replicate games. Definition 1 forbids consulting the network's own behaviour, yet Track A permits iterative self-testing and per-disagreement override tables (offline solve baked into weights), so Track A results include tabulation. Reported boundary: one-ply-checkable tactics compile exactly; multi-move planning does not in a single forward pass.
